subject.title: Feature: enrich usage/status JSON with agent, cron, and channel labels

question: Should OpenClaw add stable cron/channel attribution fields to official status and sessions-usage JSON now, and what privacy-safe field shape should be public?
rationale: Current main already exposes some attribution but not the requested cron identity or target-kind contract, and adding those fields creates durable public JSON/API semantics that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve a narrow additive JSON contract
options.body: Add optional status/usage row fields for cron job id/name and channel/target kind while keeping raw private target ids omitted or behind an explicit opt-in.

options.title: Defer to existing APIs and docs
options.body: Keep current `status --json` and `sessions.usage` fields as the supported path and document that dashboards must join cron/session metadata locally.

options.title: Fold into broader telemetry design
options.body: Track this with broader usage/event-stream observability so status JSON, sessions.usage, and WebSocket attribution use one shared contract.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow additive JSON contract
recommendation.body: Add optional status/usage row fields for cron job id/name and channel/target kind while keeping raw private target ids omitted or behind an explicit opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses recent status, Gateway API, and cron owner-attribution history where steipete has the strongest current-main signal.
